sources.quote: כי אילו היה מושבך גבוה כקן העוף לא יצילך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says even a dwelling high as a bird's nest would not save you.

24:23.headline: El: 'God', or 'these things'?
24:23.body: אל usually means God. Rashi reads it as 'these' (אלה): who can survive when He brings these things about, when Sennacherib throws the nations into chaos; Ibn Ezra offers that it is the king of Assyria, who set himself up as a god.

sources.quote: מִי יָכוֹל לְהַחֲיוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ מִשּׂוּמוֹ אֶת אֵלֶּה
sources.says: Rashi says: who can keep himself alive when He sets these things in place.

sources.quote: שֶׁיַּעֲמֹד סַנְחֵרִיב וִיבַלְבֵּל אֶת כָּל הָאֻמּוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says these things are Sennacherib rising and throwing all nations into confusion.

sources.quote: הטעם על מלך אשור ששם נפשו כמו אל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it refers to the king of Assyria, who made himself like a god.

24:24.headline: Tzim: great ships coming from Kittim
24:24.body: Rashi and Rashbam read צים as great ships, like 'a mighty ship (צי)' in Isaiah. Onkelos renders it as bands of men from Rome.

sources.quote: וצים. סְפִינוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says צים are great ships.

sources.quote: וצים - כמו: וצי אדיר
sources.says: Rashbam compares 'and a mighty ship'.

sources.quote: וְסִיעַן יִצְטָרְחַן מֵרוֹמָאֵי
sources.says: Onkelos renders: and bands will gather from the Romans.

25:1.headline: 'He settled' is a warning that trouble is coming
25:1.body: The chapter opens with וישב, 'Israel settled'. Rabbi Yochanan says that wherever the Torah uses this word, pain follows, and his first proof is this verse: settling at Shittim leads straight into sin.

sources.quote: כל מקום שנאמר ״וישב״ אינו אלא לשון צער, שנאמר: ״וישב ישראל בשטים
sources.says: Rabbi Yochanan says that every place the Torah says 'and he settled' means trouble, and he cites this verse first.

25:1.headline: 'Began', or 'made their holiness ordinary'?
25:1.body: ויחל plainly means the people 'began' to go after Moabite women. Rabbeinu Bahya and Or HaChaim also hear חול, ordinary or profane, in it: the people turned their holiness into something common.

sources.quote: ויחל העם. עשה קדושתו חול, כלשון (בראשית ט׳:כ׳) ויחל נח
sources.says: Bahya says the people made their holiness profane, using the word the same way as 'Noah began' in Genesis.

sources.quote: אמרו ויחל לשון חלול, שנתחלל לזנות
sources.says: Or HaChaim cites the sages that ויחל means profaning: the people profaned themselves by going astray.

25:3.headline: Yoked to Peor, but not stuck to it
25:3.body: ויצמד comes from צמד, a pair of oxen under one yoke. Rabbeinu Bahya says being yoked is a looser bond than cleaving: Israel was attached to Peor like a bracelet on a hand, but cleaves to God for real.

sources.quote: ויצמד ישראל. מגזרת צמד בקר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word comes from a yoked pair of oxen.

sources.quote: ויש חלוק בין לשון הצמדה ולשון דבקות
sources.says: Bahya says there is a difference between being yoked and cleaving.

sources.quote: הנצמדים לבעל פעור כצמידים על ידי אשה, ואתם הדבקים דבקים ממש
sources.says: Bahya quotes the sages: those yoked to Peor were like bracelets on a woman's hand, but those who cleave to God truly cleave.

25:3.headline: Peor is named for its crude form of worship
25:3.body: Rashi links פעור to פער, to open wide. He says the idol was worshipped by people baring themselves before it and relieving themselves, and that this was its service.

sources.quote: על שם שפוערין לפניו פי הטבעת ומוציאין רעי, וזו היא עבודתו
sources.says: Rashi says it is named for the way worshippers exposed themselves and relieved themselves before it, which was its worship.

25:8.headline: An unusual word for a tent that Ibn Ezra hears in Arabic
25:8.body: Rashi says הקבה, where Pinchas followed the man, means the tent. Ibn Ezra agrees and says a close word exists in the language of Kedar, his name for Arabic.

sources.quote: אל הקבה. אל האהל
sources.says: Rashi says the word means the tent.

sources.quote: כמו אל האהל וכן קרוב בלשון קדר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means the tent, and a close word exists in the language of Kedar.

25:8.headline: Into the tent, and into her belly
25:8.body: Pinchas enters the קבה, the tent, and stabs the woman אל קבתה, nearly the same word. Rashi reads it as her belly, like the stomach portion given to priests, while Ibn Ezra also records 'in her tent'.

sources.quote: אל קבתה. כמו "והלחיים והקבה"
sources.says: Rashi says the word is the same as the stomach in the list of the priest's portions.

sources.quote: בקובה שהיתה שם עם אחי זמרי. וי"א כי קבתה מגזרת הזרוע והלחיים והקבה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra gives two readings: in the tent where Zimri's brothers were, or the stomach, as in the priest's portions.

sources.quote: הקבה כנגד ואת האשה אל קבתה
sources.says: Bahya says the priests receive the stomach portion as a reward for Pinchas stabbing the woman in her belly.

26:5.headline: God's name wraps each clan name, ה in front, י behind
26:5.body: Each clan name in this list is written with ה before it and י after it. Rashi says these two letters spell God's name, יה, as a witness that every family really comes from its fathers, even after Egypt.

sources.quote: לְפִיכָךְ הִטִּיל הַקָּבָּ"ה שְׁמוֹ עֲלֵיהֶם — ה"א מִצַּד זֶה וְיוֹ"ד מִצַּד זֶה
sources.says: Rashi says God put His name on them, a ה on one side and a י on the other.

sources.quote: לוֹמַר, מֵעִיד אֲנִי עֲלֵיהֶם שֶׁהֵם בְּנֵי אֲבוֹתֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the name testifies that they are the sons of their fathers.

sources.quote: וְחָתַם עֲלֵיהֶם שֵׁם יָ״הּ, כִּי שֵׁם זֶה הוּא מְתַוֵּךְ בֵּין אִישׁ לְאִשָּׁה
sources.says: Kli Yakar says the name יה is sealed on them because it stands between husband and wife.

26:10.headline: לנס: a warning sign, or a banner raised in honor?
26:10.body: Rashi and Ralbag read נס as a sign and a reminder, warning anyone who would fight the priesthood. The Netziv reads it as 'raised high': the rebels' fire pans became plating for the altar.

sources.quote: ויהיו לנס. לְאוֹת וּלְזִכָּרוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says it means a sign and a reminder, so no outsider would again challenge the priesthood.

sources.ref: Ralbag Beur HaMilot on Torah, Numbers 26:10:1
sources.quote: שהיו לאות ולזכרון לבני ישראל להזהירם שלא יקרב איש אשר לא מזרע אהרן
sources.says: Ralbag says they became a sign to warn Israel that no one outside Aaron's family may serve in the sanctuary.

sources.quote: פי׳ גבוה במעלה שזכו לשם טוב במה שצוה הקב״ה לעשות מן המחתות צפוי למזבח
sources.says: The Netziv says it means raised high: they earned a good name when their fire pans were made into the altar's covering.

26:13.headline: Zerah and Tzochar: one man, two names of light
26:13.body: In Genesis this son of Simeon is called צחר. Rashi and Ramban say Zerah is the same man, and explain צחר as צהר, light. זרח also speaks of light: it is the word for the sun rising.

sources.quote: לזרח. הוּא צֹחַר, לְשׁוֹן צֹהַר
sources.says: Rashi says Zerah is Tzochar, a word related to צהר, light.

sources.quote: לְזֶרַח הוּא צוֹחַר (בראשית מו י) לְשׁוֹן צֹהַר
sources.says: Ramban repeats that Zerah is the Tzochar of Genesis, from the word for light.

26:16.headline: Etzbon became Ozni, and both names mean 'listen'
26:16.body: Rashi says the clan of אזני is Gad's son Etzbon from Genesis, but does not know why the name changed. Or HaChaim cites a midrash: both names mean listening, from אצית and האזין, so it is really the same name.

sources.quote: אוֹמֵר אֲנִי שֶׁזּוֹ מִשְׁפַּחַת אֶצְבּוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says this is the family of Etzbon, and he does not know why it is not called by his name.

sources.quote: מִלְּשׁוֹן אֲצֵית וְהֶאֱזִין
sources.says: Or HaChaim quotes the Pesikta that Ozni is Etzbon, both from words meaning to listen.

sources.quote: וְאֵין הַכָּתוּב מַקְפִּיד עַל שִׁנּוּי הַשֵּׁם כְּשֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּמַשְׁמָעוֹ שֵׁם הָרִאשׁוֹן
sources.says: Or HaChaim says Scripture does not mind a changed name when it keeps the first name's meaning.

26:24.headline: Yov becomes Yashuv, borrowing a letter from his father
26:24.body: In Genesis this son of Issachar is called יוב. Chizkuni says he gained a ש from his father's name, יששכר, which has two of them.

sources.quote: לישוב. הוּא יוֹב הָאָמוּר בְּיוֹרְדֵי מִצְרַיִם
sources.says: Rashi says Yashuv is the Yov listed among those who went down to Egypt.

sources.quote: לישוב הוא יוב שנתוספה לו שי״‎ן אחת משני שיני״‎ן שבשם אביו
sources.says: Chizkuni says one of the two letters ש in his father's name was added to Yov's name.

26:38.headline: Achiram: named for a brother who rose high
26:38.body: In Genesis this son of Benjamin is called אחי. Rashi says the name אחירם is for Joseph: Benjamin's brother (אח) who was raised (רם) above him.

sources.quote: וּלְפִי שֶׁנִּקְרָא עַל שֵׁם יוֹסֵף שֶׁהָיָה אָחִיו וְרָם מִמֶּנּוּ נִקְרָא אֲחִירָם
sources.says: Rashi says he was named for Joseph, his brother who was higher than him, so he is called Achiram.

26:44.headline: One clan name already carries God's name inside it
26:44.body: Every other clan here gets ה in front and י at the end. Rashi says ימנה did not need them, since its name already starts with י and ends with ה. Ibn Ezra notes the clan is called הימנה, not הימיני.

sources.quote: אֲבָל בְּיִמְנָה לֹא הֻצְרַךְ לוֹמַר "מִשְׁפַּחַת הַיִּמְנִי" לְפִי שֶׁהַשֵּׁם קָבוּעַ בּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says ימנה did not need the extra letters because the name is already fixed in it.

sources.quote: לימנה משפחת הימנה ואיננו הימיני
sources.says: Ibn Ezra notes the clan of Yimnah is called הימנה, not הימיני.

26:46.headline: Was Serah Asher's daughter, or his wife's?
26:46.body: Rashi says Serah is listed because she was still alive. Ramban reports that Onkelos calls her the daughter of Asher's wife. She was his stepdaughter, so she could inherit land, and that is why she is counted here.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁהָיְתָה קַיֶּמֶת בְּחַיֶּיהָ מְנָאָהּ כָּאן
sources.says: Rashi says she was counted here because she was still alive.

sources.quote: אֲבָל הָיְתָה בַּת אִשְׁתּוֹ מֵאִישׁ אַחֵר, לֹא הָיָה לוֹ בֵּן וְהָיְתָה נַחֲלָתוֹ לְבִתּוֹ
sources.says: Ramban says she was Asher's wife's daughter by another man, who had no son, so his land went to her.

sources.quote: לפי שגדלה בתוך ביתו והיתה נקראת על שמו
sources.says: Chizkuni says she was called Asher's daughter because she grew up in his house.

26:55.headline: 'Only by lot': the small word that leaves out Joshua and Caleb
26:55.body: Rashi stops on אך, 'only', a word that limits. He says it leaves out Joshua and Caleb, who got their land by God's word and not by lot.

sources.quote: אך בגורל. יָצְאוּ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְכָלֵב
sources.says: Rashi says 'only by lot' excludes Joshua and Caleb.

sources.quote: אך יצאו יהושע וכלב שלא נטלו בגורל
sources.says: Chizkuni says אך excludes Joshua and Caleb, who did not take their share by lot.

26:56.headline: 'By the mouth of the lot': the lot itself spoke
26:56.body: על פי usually means 'according to', but פי is also 'mouth'. Rashi says the lot really spoke and called out which tribe got which land. Bekhor Shor reads it as 'by mouth and by lot': the priest named the land, and the lot agreed.

sources.quote: על פי הגורל. הַגּוֹרָל הָיָה מְדַבֵּר
sources.says: Rashi says the lot was speaking.

sources.quote: וְהַגּוֹרָל עַצְמוֹ הָיָה צוֹוֵחַ וְאוֹמֵר אֲנִי הַגּוֹרָל עָלִיתִי
sources.says: Rashi says the lot itself cried out, 'I, the lot, came up for this border and this tribe'.

sources.quote: על פי הגורל. על פה וגורל
sources.says: Bekhor Shor reads it as 'by mouth and by lot', the priest speaking and the lot matching.

26:59.headline: Born in Egypt: Yocheved arrived just as the family did
26:59.body: Rashi reads 'born in Egypt' closely: she was conceived before, and born as the family entered Egypt's walls. That makes her the seventieth person who went down. Ralbag says the words do not force this reading.

sources.quote: לֵדָתָהּ בְּמִצְרַיִם וְאֵין הוֹרָתָהּ בְּמִצְרַיִם, כְּשֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ לְתוֹךְ הַחוֹמָה יְלָדַתָּה
sources.says: Rashi says she was born in Egypt but not conceived there; she was born as they came within the walls.

sources.quote: וְהִיא הִשְׁלִימָה מִנְיַן שִׁבְעִים
sources.says: Rashi says she completed the count of seventy.

sources.ref: Ralbag Beur HaMilot on Torah, Numbers 26:59:1
sources.quote: שלא תהיה הורתה גם כן במצרים כמו שלא יחייב אמרו ויולד ליוסף בארץ מצרים
sources.says: Ralbag says the verse does not mean she was not also conceived in Egypt, just as with Joseph's sons born in Egypt.

26:64.headline: 'Not a man was left', but the women were
26:64.body: Rashi reads איש as 'man', not 'person'. The decree after the spies fell only on the men, he says, because the women loved the land and asked for a share in it.

sources.quote: אֲבָל עַל הַנָּשִׁים לֹא נִגְזְרָה גְזֵרַת הַמְרַגְּלִים, לְפִי שֶׁהֵן הָיוּ מְחַבְּבוֹת אֶת הָאָרֶץ
sources.says: Rashi says the spies' decree was not made against the women, because they loved the land.

sources.quote: וּבְאֵלֶּה לֹא הָיָה אִישׁ. אֲבָל נָשִׁים הָיוּ
sources.says: Kli Yakar says no men were left, but women were.

27:3.headline: 'He died in his own sin': which sin, and what did it cause?
27:3.body: Rashi says the daughters mean their father died for his own sin alone, not as one of Korah's rebels, and the sages guess which sin it was. Ibn Ezra cites Rabbi Yehudah HaLevi, who reads 'in his sin' with the next words: because of his sin he had no sons.

sources.quote: אֶלָּא בְּחֶטְאוֹ לְבַדּוֹ מֵת, וְלֹא הֶחֱטִיא אֶת אֲחֵרִים עִמּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says he died for his own sin alone and did not lead others to sin with him.

sources.quote: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר מְקוֹשֵׁשׁ עֵצִים הָיָה
sources.says: Rashi cites Rabbi Akiva, who says he was the man who gathered wood on the Sabbath.

sources.quote: כי פי' כי בחטאו מת דבק עם ובנים לא היו לו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites Rabbi Yehudah HaLevi, who joins 'in his sin he died' to 'and he had no sons'.

27:7.headline: God answers the daughters: 'כן', meaning 'they are right'
27:7.body: כן usually means 'so' or 'thus'. Onkelos and Rashi read it as 'rightly': the daughters saw what Moses did not, and Rashi adds, happy is the one whose words God agrees with.

sources.quote: מַגִּיד שֶׁרָאֲתָה עֵינָן מַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה
sources.says: Rashi, following Onkelos's 'rightly', says this shows their eyes saw what Moses' eye did not.

sources.quote: יָאוּת בְּנַת צְלָפְחָד מְמַלְּלָן
sources.says: Onkelos translates: the daughters of Zelophehad speak rightly.

sources.quote: אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם שֶׁהַקָּבָּ"ה מוֹדֶה לִדְבָרָיו
sources.says: Rashi says happy is the person whose words God agrees with.

27:7.headline: 'Give, you shall give': the doubled verb means two shares
27:7.body: The verse doubles the verb, נתן תתן. Rashi says the daughters received two shares: their father's own portion, and his share in his father Hepher's land.

sources.quote: שְׁנֵי חֲלָקִים, חֵלֶק אֲבִיהֶן שֶׁהָיָה מִיּוֹצְאֵי מִצְרַיִם, וְחֶלְקוֹ עִם אֶחָיו בְּנִכְסֵי חֵפֶר
sources.says: Rashi says it means two portions: their father's own share as one who left Egypt, and his share with his brothers in Hepher's property.

sources.quote: נתן תתן להם אחוזת נחלה וגו'. שני חלקים
sources.says: Bahya also reads the doubled verb as two portions.

27:18.headline: 'A man with spirit in him': prophecy, or patience with people?
27:18.body: Every living person has a spirit, so what does it mean here? Onkelos says the spirit of prophecy, while Rashi says Joshua could meet each person's spirit on its own terms.

sources.quote: גְּבַר דִּי רוּחַ נְבוּאָה בֵיהּ
sources.says: Onkelos translates: a man in whom is the spirit of prophecy.

sources.quote: שֶׁיּוּכַל לַהֲלֹךְ כְּנֶגֶד רוּחוֹ שֶׁל כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
sources.says: Rashi says it means he can deal with the spirit of every single person.

sources.quote: וכל איש חי יש בו רוח
sources.says: Ibn Ezra points out that every living man has a spirit, so the verse must mean something more, like strength.

27:20.headline: 'Some of your glory', not all of it: the sun and the moon
27:20.body: God tells Moses to give Joshua מהודך, 'from your glory'. Rashi reads the 'from' as 'some, not all': Moses' face was like the sun, and Joshua's like the moon.

sources.quote: וְלֹא כָּל הוֹדְךָ, וּמָצִינוּ לְמֵדִין פְּנֵי מֹשֶׁה כַּחַמָּה פְּנֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כַּלְּבָנָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means some of your glory, not all of it: Moses' face was like the sun, Joshua's like the moon.

sources.quote: וְתִתֵּן מִזִּיוָךְ עֲלוֹהִי
sources.says: Onkelos translates: and you shall put some of your radiance on him.

28:2.headline: 'Guard' the offering: stand beside it, or check it
28:2.body: Rashi says 'you shall guard' means priests, Levites and ordinary Israelites must stand by the daily offering, which is where the groups of standers (מעמדות) came from. Chizkuni says it means checking the animal for flaws ahead of time, as with the Passover lamb.

sources.quote: שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כֹּהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם וְיִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹמְדִין עַל גַּבָּיו, מִכָּאן לָמְדוּ וְתִקְּנוּ מַעֲמָדוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says priests, Levites and Israelites must stand over it, and from here the sages set up the standing groups.

sources.quote: מה שמירה האמורה גבי פסח בקור אף שמירה האמורה כאן בקור
sources.says: Chizkuni says that just as 'guarding' the Passover lamb means inspecting it, so does 'guarding' here.

28:7.headline: A 'strong drink' poured on the altar means real wine
28:7.body: שכר is the word for strong drink. Rashi says here it means wine strong enough to make you drunk, not wine fresh from the press, and Onkelos says 'aged wine'; Ramban says it rules out wine mixed with water.

sources.quote: יַיִן הַמְשַׁכֵּר, פְּרָט לְיַיִן מִגִּתּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means wine that intoxicates, excluding wine straight from the press.

sources.quote: נִסּוּךְ דַּחֲמַר עַתִּיק
sources.says: Onkelos translates it 'a pouring of aged wine'.

sources.quote: אֲבָל שֵׁכָר – לְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַמָּזוּג
sources.says: Ramban says the word comes to exclude diluted wine.

28:8.headline: A 'pleasing smell' means God is content
28:8.body: ריח ניחח is literally 'a pleasing smell'. Rashi reads it as contentment (נחת רוח): God is pleased that what He said was done, and Onkelos renders it 'accepted with favor'.

sources.quote: נַחַת רוּחַ לְפָנַי שֶׁאָמַרְתִּי וְנַעֲשָׂה רְצוֹנִי
sources.says: Rashi says it means contentment before God, that He spoke and His will was done.

sources.quote: קֻרְבַּן דְּמִתְקַבַּל בְּרַעֲוָא
sources.says: Onkelos translates it 'an offering accepted with favor'.

28:18.headline: A 'holy calling' or a 'holy occasion'?
28:18.body: מקרא looks like it comes from קרא, 'to call'. Chizkuni, following Onkelos, reads it as מקרה, 'an occasion': mark the day as special with food, drink and clean clothes.

sources.quote: מקרא קודש לשון מקרה כתרגומו קרי מערעי במאכל ובמשתה ובכסות נקיה
sources.says: Chizkuni says מקרא means an occasion, as Onkelos translates it, to be marked with food, drink and clean clothes.

sources.quote: בְּיוֹמָא קַדְמָאָה מְעָרַע קַדִּישׁ
sources.says: Onkelos translates it 'on the first day, a holy occasion'.

28:26.headline: Shavuot's other name: the Day of First Fruits
28:26.body: Here Shavuot is called 'the day of the first fruits'. Rashi says the name comes from the two loaves brought that day, the first offering made from the new wheat.

sources.quote: חַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת קָרוּי בִּכּוּרֵי קְצִיר חִטִּים עַל שֵׁם שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם
sources.says: Rashi says Shavuot is called the first fruits of the wheat harvest because of the two loaves.

29:19.headline: Three odd spellings hide the word 'water'
29:19.body: The wording changes on three days: ונסכיהם on day two, ונסכיה on day six, כמשפטם on day seven. The extra letters are mem, yod, mem, which spell מים, water. Rashi says this hints at the water poured on the altar at Sukkot.

sources.quote: בשני ונסכיהם, בששי ונסכיה, בשביעי כמשפטם, מם יוד מם הרי כאן מים, רמז לנסוך המים מן התורה בחג
sources.says: Rashi says the extra letters on the second, sixth and seventh days spell מים, a hint in the Torah to the water libation on Sukkot.

29:35.headline: Atzeret: a day of stopping work, or of staying on
29:35.body: עצרת comes from 'hold back'. Rashi gives two readings. Hold back from work. Or hold back from leaving: stay one more night. He adds the midrash that God asks Israel for one small meal of their own.

sources.quote: עצורים בעשית מלאכה
sources.says: Rashi says it means held back from doing work.

sources.quote: עצרו מלצאת, מלמד שטעון לינה
sources.says: Rashi also says it means hold back from leaving, teaching that one must stay the night.

sources.quote: עשו לי סעודה קטנה כדי שאהנה מכם
sources.says: Rashi quotes the midrash: God says, make Me a small meal so I can enjoy you.

3:1.headline: Moses' 'offspring' are Aaron's sons, because he taught them
3:1.body: The verse promises the offspring of Aaron and Moses but lists only Aaron's sons. Rashi says they count as Moses' too because he taught them Torah: teaching someone's child is like giving birth to him.

sources.quote: וְנִקְרְאוּ תוֹלְדוֹת מֹשֶׁה, לְפִי שֶׁלִּמְּדָן תּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says they are called Moses' offspring because he taught them Torah.

sources.quote: שֶׁכָּל הַמְלַמֵּד אֶת בֶּן חֲבֵרוֹ תּוֹרָה מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִלּוּ יְלָדוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says whoever teaches another's son Torah is regarded by Scripture as if he had fathered him.

sources.quote: כי תלמידיו של אדם הן הן תולדותיו העקריות
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says a person's students are his truest offspring.

3:4.headline: 'Al pnei Aharon': in Aaron's lifetime, or before his eyes?
3:4.body: Rashi reads על פני as 'in his lifetime'. Ramban objects that every priest serves in his father's lifetime, and reads it as Nadav and Avihu dying in front of their father, as Chronicles says 'before their father'.

sources.quote: על פני אהרן. בְּחַיָּיו
sources.says: Rashi says 'al pnei Aharon' means in Aaron's lifetime.

sources.quote: כִּי כָל אִישׁ מִבְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֲנִים יְכַהֵן בְּחַיֵּי אָבִיו
sources.says: Ramban objects that any son of Aaron serves as priest in his father's lifetime.

sources.quote: וַיָּמָת נָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא לִפְנֵי ה' עַל פְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן אֲבִיהֶם בְּהַקְרִיבָם אֵשׁ זָרָה
sources.says: Ramban reads it as: Nadav and Avihu died before God, in front of Aaron their father, when they offered strange fire.

sources.quote: וַיָּמָת נָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא לִפְנֵי אֲבִיהֶם
sources.says: Ramban cites Chronicles: Nadav and Avihu died before their father.

3:10.headline: Tifkod: in a counting chapter, here it means 'appoint'
3:10.body: פקד is the verb for counting all through this chapter. Rashi and Rashbam say that here it means appointing Aaron and his sons to office, as 'the captain of the guard appointed (ויפקד) Joseph'.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן פְּקִידוּת, וְאֵינוֹ לְשׁוֹן מִנְיָן
sources.says: Rashi says it means appointment, not counting.

sources.quote: תעשהו פקיד וממונה עליהם. כמו: ויפקד שר הטבחים את יוסף
sources.says: Rashbam says: make him an officer in charge, as in 'the captain of the guard appointed Joseph'.

sources.quote: וְיָת אַהֲרֹן וְיָת בְּנוֹהִי תְּמַנֵּי
sources.says: Onkelos renders: and Aaron and his sons you shall appoint.

3:12.headline: The Levites took the firstborns' place after the golden calf
3:12.body: Rashi says the service first belonged to the firstborn. When they sinned with the golden calf they lost it, and the Levites, who had not worshipped the idol, were chosen in their place.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁהָיְתָה הָעֲבוֹדָה בַּבְּכוֹרוֹת, וּכְשֶׁחָטְאוּ בָעֵגֶל נִפְסְלוּ, וְהַלְוִיִּם שֶׁלֹּא עָבְדוּ עֲ"זָ נִבְחֲרוּ תַחְתֵּיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the service was with the firstborn; when they sinned with the calf they were disqualified, and the Levites, who did not worship idols, were chosen instead.

sources.quote: מִקֶּדֶם הָיְתָה הָעֲבוֹדָה בַּבְּכוֹרוֹת
sources.says: Sforno also says the service was once done by the firstborn.

3:15.headline: Levites counted from one month old: why so young
3:15.body: Rashi says that at one month a baby is past the danger of dying as a newborn and can be called a guardian of the holy; a midrash he cites adds that this tribe was counted even from the womb. Rashbam says it matches the firstborn they replace, who are redeemed from one month.

sources.quote: מִשֶּׁיָּצָא מִכְּלַל נְפָלִים הוּא נִמְנֶה לִקָּרֵא שׁוֹמֵר מִשְׁמֶרֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says once a baby is past the risk of dying newborn, he is counted and called a keeper of the holy charge.

sources.quote: לָמוּד הוּא אוֹתוֹ הַשֵּׁבֶט לִהְיוֹת נִמְנֶה מִן הַבֶּטֶן
sources.says: Rashi cites a midrash that this tribe was used to being counted from the womb.

sources.quote: לפי שהיו באים לפטור את הבכורות שחייבין בפדיון מבן חדש ומעלה, לכן גם מניינם מבן חדש
sources.says: Rashbam says the Levites came to release the firstborn, who are redeemed from one month, so they were counted from one month too.

3:16.headline: Counting babies 'by the mouth of God': a voice from each tent
3:16.body: Moses asked how he could go into people's tents to count their nursing infants. Rashi brings a midrash: Moses stood at each tent door, and a heavenly voice from inside announced how many babies were there.

sources.quote: הֵיאַךְ אֲנִי נִכְנָס לְתוֹךְ אָהֳלֵיהֶם לָדַעַת מִנְיַן יוֹנְקֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says Moses asked how he could enter their tents to know the number of their nursing babies.

sources.quote: וּבַת קוֹל יוֹצְאָה מִן הָאֹהֶל וְאוֹמֶרֶת כָּךְ וָכָךְ תִּינוֹקוֹת יֵשׁ בְּאֹהֶל זֶה, לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר עַל פִּי ה'
sources.says: Rashi says a heavenly voice came from the tent saying how many infants were in it, and that is why it says 'by the mouth of God'.

3:31.headline: 'The screen': the inner curtain, or the Tent's door?
3:31.body: Rashi says this מסך is the inner curtain, the פרכת, which is also called 'the curtain of the screen'. Ibn Ezra says many got this wrong: it is the screen at the entrance to the Tent.

sources.quote: הִיא הַפָּרֹכֶת, שֶׁאַף הִיא קְרוּיָה פָּרֹכֶת הַמָּסָךְ
sources.says: Rashi says it is the parochet, which is also called the curtain of the screen.

sources.quote: ורבים השתבשו בפירוש והמסך וכל עבודתו והאמת ברורה שהוא מסך פתח אהל מועד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says many erred in explaining 'the screen'; the truth is that it is the screen at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

3:39.headline: Dots over 'and Aaron': he was not in the Levite count
3:39.body: The word ואהרן here is written with dots over its letters. Rashi says the dots show that Aaron was not part of the count of the Levites.

sources.quote: נָקוּד עַל וְאַהֲרֹן, לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּמִנְיַן הַלְוִיִּם
sources.says: Rashi says there are dots on 'and Aaron' to say he was not among those counted as Levites.

30:3.headline: Do not 'profane' your word, or do not 'delay' it?
30:3.body: Rashi reads יחל as 'profane': a person must not make his word into something cheap. Rashbam says that is wrong by the plain sense: it means 'wait', as in 'he waited' (ויחל), so one must not put off keeping a vow.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ לֹא יְחַלֵּל דְּבָרוֹ — לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה דְּבָרוֹ חֻלִּין
sources.says: Rashi says it means he must not profane his word, not treat it as ordinary.

sources.quote: לא יאחר את נדרו עד לאחר הרגלים
sources.says: Rashbam says it means he must not delay his vow past the pilgrim festivals.

sources.quote: והמפרש לשון חלול לפי הפשט טעות הוא בידו
sources.says: Rashbam says that whoever reads it as 'profane' is mistaken by the plain sense.

31:3.headline: Not just 'men': here the word means righteous men
31:3.body: Rashi says אנשים here means righteous men, as when Moses told Joshua to 'choose us men'. Ramban explains why that mattered: many had sinned with the women of Moab and were not fit to carry out God's revenge.

sources.quote: אנשים. צַדִּיקִים, וְכֵן "בְּחַר לָנוּ אֲנָשִׁים
sources.says: Rashi says 'men' here means righteous men, as in 'choose us men' (Exodus 17).

sources.quote: כִּי הַנִּכְשָׁלִים בִּבְנוֹת מוֹאָב הָיוּ רַבִּים וְאֵינָם רְאוּיִים לְנִקְמַת ה', עַל כֵּן בָּחֲרוּ אֲנָשִׁים צַדִּיקִים וִידוּעִים לְשִׁבְטֵיהֶם
sources.says: Ramban says many had stumbled with the women of Moab and were unfit for God's revenge, so they chose righteous men known to their tribes.

31:3.headline: God calls it Israel's revenge; Moses calls it God's
31:3.body: In verse 2 God says 'avenge the Israelites', but here Moses says 'the LORD's vengeance'. Chizkuni gives Moses' reason: the nations hate Israel only because of God, so the revenge is His.

sources.quote: הקב״‎ה אומר נקמת בני ישראל ומשה אומר נקמת ה׳‎ אמר משה רבונו של עולם הנקמה שלך היא שאין הכנענים שונאים אותנו אלא בשבילך
sources.says: Chizkuni says God said 'Israel's vengeance' and Moses said 'the LORD's vengeance', telling God the revenge is His, since the nations hate Israel only because of Him.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָעוֹמֵד כְּנֶגֶד יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּאִלּוּ עוֹמֵד כְּנֶגֶד הַקָּבָּ"ה
sources.says: Rashi says whoever stands against Israel is as if he stands against God.

31:5.headline: 'Handed over': the soldiers did not want to go
31:5.body: וימסרו means they were handed over, not that they stepped forward. Rashi says the men refused to go because they had heard Moses would die once Midian was punished, so they had to be sent against their will.

sources.quote: וּמִשֶּׁשָּׁמְעוּ שֶׁמִּיתַת מֹשֶׁה תְלוּיָה בְנִקְמַת מִדְיָן לֹא רָצוּ לָלֶכֶת עַד שֶׁנִּמְסְרוּ עַל כָּרְחָן
sources.says: Rashi says once they heard Moses' death depended on the revenge against Midian, they would not go until they were handed over against their will.

sources.quote: וימסרו - בעל כרחן, לפי שאמר הקדוש ברוך הוא: ואחר תאסף אל עמך
sources.says: Rashbam says they went against their will, because God had said Moses would then be gathered to his people.

31:8.headline: Kings who fell out of the sky onto the dead
31:8.body: על חלליהם can mean 'with their slain' or 'on top of their slain'. Rashi tells a midrash: Balaam made Midian's kings fly by sorcery, and when they were shown the gold plate bearing God's name they fell onto the bodies below.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיָה בִּלְעָם עִמָּהֶם וּמַפְרִיחַ מַלְכֵי מִדְיָן בִּכְשָׁפִים וְהוּא עַצְמוֹ פוֹרֵחַ עִמָּהֶם, הֶרְאָה לָהֶם אֶת הַצִּיץ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם חָקוּק בּוֹ וְהֵם נוֹפְלִים, לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר "עַל חַלְלֵיהֶם" בְּמַלְכֵי מִדְיָן — שֶׁנּוֹפְלִים עַל הַחֲלָלִים מִן הָאֲוִיר
sources.says: Rashi says Balaam made the kings of Midian fly by sorcery; shown the headplate engraved with God's name, they fell onto the slain from the air.

sources.quote: על חלליהם עם חלליהם
sources.says: Chizkuni reads it plainly as 'with their slain'.

31:8.headline: Balaam took Israel's weapon, words, so Israel took his
31:8.body: Rashi says Israel wins with its mouth, by prayer, while the nations win with the sword. Balaam tried to beat Israel with his mouth by cursing them, so Israel came against him with the sword.

sources.quote: הוּא בָא עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהֶחֱלִיף אֻמָּנוּתוֹ בְּאֻמָּנוּתָם, שֶׁאֵין נוֹצְחִים אֶלָּא בְּפִיהֶם וְעַל יְדֵי תְפִלָּה וּבַקָּשָׁה
sources.says: Rashi says Balaam came against Israel and swapped his craft for theirs, since they win only with their mouths, through prayer and request.

sources.quote: אַף הֵם בָּאוּ עָלָיו וְהֶחֱלִיפוּ אֻמָּנוּתָם בְּאֻמָּנוּת הָאֻמּוֹת שֶׁבָּאִין בַּחֶרֶב
sources.says: Rashi says Israel in turn swapped their craft for that of the nations, who come with the sword.

31:21.headline: Eleazar teaches the law because Moses, angry, forgot it
31:21.body: Here Eleazar the priest teaches the law, not Moses. Rashi says Moses had grown angry at the officers, and anger made him forget the rules for cleaning gentile vessels, just as anger led him to strike the rock.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁבָּא מֹשֶׁה לִכְלַל כַּעַס בָּא לִכְלַל טָעוּת, שֶׁנִּתְעַלְּמוּ מִמֶּנּוּ הִלְכוֹת גִּעוּלֵי גּוֹיִם
sources.says: Rashi says because Moses came to anger, he came to error: the laws of purging gentile vessels slipped from him.

sources.quote: וְכֵן בְּשִׁמְעוּ נָא הַמֹּרִים (במדבר כ') "וַיַּךְ אֶת הַסֶּלַע" — עַל יְדֵי הַכַּעַס טָעָה
sources.says: Rashi says the same happened at 'Listen, you rebels', when Moses struck the rock: through anger he erred.

31:22.headline: 'Only' the metal: scrape off the rust first
31:22.body: אך usually means 'only' or 'but'. Rashi says it limits using the vessels until they are purged, and the sages read it as 'only the bare metal', so the rust must come off before purging.

sources.quote: וְ"אַךְ" לְשׁוֹן מִעוּט, כְּלוֹמַר מְמֻעָטִין אַתֶּם מִלְּהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בַּכֵּלִים אֲפִלּוּ לְאַחַר טָהֲרָתָן מִטֻּמְאַת הַמֵּת
sources.says: Rashi says אך is a limiting word: you are held back from using the vessels even after they are cleansed of corpse impurity.

sources.quote: שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהַעֲבִיר חֲלוּדָה שֶׁלּוֹ קֹדֶם שֶׁיַּגְעִילֶנּוּ, וְזֶהוּ לְשׁוֹן אך, שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא שָׁם חֲלוּדָה אַךְ הַמַּתֶּכֶת יִהְיֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא
sources.says: Rashi says the sages learn that rust must be removed before purging: 'only' the metal as it is, with no rust.

31:23.headline: 'Water of niddah': ash water, or a ritual bath?
31:23.body: מי נדה usually means the water mixed with red heifer ash. Ibn Ezra says that is how it looks to him, but the sages read it as enough water for a woman's ritual bath, and he defers to them.

sources.quote: היה נראה לנו כי הוא מי אפר הפרה כמו מי נדה לא זורק עליו וחז"ל אמרו כי טעמו בשיעור המים שתרחץ בהם האשה הנדה ודעתם רחבה מדעתינו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it seemed to mean the red heifer's ash water, but the sages said it means the amount of water a niddah bathes in, and their knowledge is wider than ours.

sources.quote: וּמֵי נִדָּה הַכְּתוּבִין כָּאן דָּרְשׁוּ מַיִם הָרְאוּיִם לִטְבֹּל בָּהֶם נִדָּה, וְכַמָּה הֵם? אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה
sources.says: Rashi says the sages read 'niddah water' here as water fit for a niddah to immerse in, which is forty se'ah.

31:49.headline: 'Not one man missing': lost in battle, or lost to sin
31:49.body: נפקד here means 'was missing', not 'was counted', as Rashi shows from other verses. Ramban adds that the sages also read it as: not one of us slipped away to sin.

sources.quote: ולא נפקד. לֹא נֶחְסַר, וְתַרְגּוּמוֹ "לָא שְׁגָא", אַף הוּא בִּלְשׁוֹן אֲרַמִי חִסָּרוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'none was lacking', and the Aramaic translation also uses a word for lacking.

sources.quote: וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דָּרְשׁוּ (שבת סד) ״וְלֹא נִפְקַד מִמֶּנּוּ אִישׁ״ - לִדְבַר עֲבֵירָה
sources.says: Ramban says the sages read 'not one man of us was missing' as referring to sin.

31:50.headline: An unknown ornament, read as jewelry for the womb
31:50.body: Ibn Ezra treats כומז as just another piece of jewelry. Rashi says it was an ornament shaped like the womb, and the gift atoned for the soldiers' thoughts about the women of Midian.

sources.quote: דְּפוּס שֶׁל בֵּית הָרֶחֶם, לְכַפֵּר הִרְהוּר הַלֵּב שֶׁל בְּנוֹת מִדְיָן
sources.says: Rashi says it was a mold of the womb, brought to atone for the heart's thoughts about the daughters of Midian.

sources.quote: וכומז. כחביריו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is like the items listed with it.

32:16.headline: Sheep pens first, children second, so Moses switches the order
32:16.body: The tribes offer to build pens for their flocks and then towns for their children. Rashi says this shows they cared more for their wealth. In verse 24 Moses answers with the children first.

sources.quote: חָסִים הָיוּ עַל מָמוֹנָם יוֹתֵר מִבְּנֵיהֶם וּבְנוֹתֵיהֶם, שֶׁהִקְדִּימוּ מִקְנֵיהֶם לְטַפָּם. אָמַר לָהֶם מֹשֶׁה "לֹא כֵן, עֲשׂוּ הָעִקָּר עִקָּר וְהַטָּפֵל טָפֵל, בְּנוּ לָכֶם תְּחִלָּה עָרִים לְטַפְּכֶם וְאַחַר כֵּן גְּדֵרוֹת לְצֹאנְכֶם
sources.says: Rashi says they cared more for their property than their children, putting cattle first, and Moses told them to build towns for their children first and pens for their flocks after.

sources.quote: הזכירו תחלה הצאן והמקנה, כי עיקר שאלתם היה בשביל המקנה
sources.says: Shadal says they named the flocks first because their whole request was about the cattle.

32:22.headline: Be clean before people too, not only before God
32:22.body: The verse says they will be "clean before God and before Israel". The sages learn from this that a person must avoid even looking guilty to others, just as he must be right before God.

sources.quote: שֶׁאָדָם צָרִיךְ לָצֵאת יְדֵי הַבִּרְיּוֹת כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לָצֵאת יְדֵי הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וִהְיִיתֶם נְקִיִים מֵיְיָ וּמִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: The Mishnah says a person must be clear in the eyes of people just as he must be clear before God, citing this verse.

sources.quote: מֵעוֹלָם לֹא נִמְצֵאת פַּת נְקִיָּה בְּיַד בְּנֵיהֶם, שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ מִמַּעֲשֵׂה לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים זֶה נִיזּוֹנִין, לְקַיֵּים מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וִהְיִיתֶם נְקִיִּים מֵה׳ וּמִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: The Talmud praises the family that baked the Temple bread: their children never had fine bread, so no one would say they ate from the holy loaves.

32:38.headline: Towns named for idols get new names
32:38.body: מוסבת שם means "the names turned". Rashi says Nevo and Baal Meon were names of idols, so the tribe of Reuben renamed those towns. Chizkuni says the names changed with each owner: Ammon and Moab, then Sichon and Og, then Israel.

sources.quote: נְבוֹ וּבַעַל מְעוֹן שְׁמוֹת עֲ"זָ הֵם, וְהָיוּ הָאֱמוֹרִיִּים קוֹרִים עָרֵיהֶם עַל שֵׁם עֲ"זָ שֶׁלָּהֶם, וּבְנֵי רְאוּבֵן הֵסֵבּוּ אֶת שְׁמָם לְשֵׁמוֹת אֲחֵרִים
sources.says: Rashi says Nevo and Baal Meon were names of idols, and the tribe of Reuben changed them to other names.

sources.quote: בתחלה נקראו בשם עמון ומואב ואח״‎כ בשם סיחון ועוג, ואח״‎כ בשם ישראל
sources.says: Chizkuni says the towns were first named by Ammon and Moab, then by Sichon and Og, and then by Israel.

32:41.headline: Yair named the villages after himself because he had no sons
32:41.body: חות means villages. Yair called the villages he captured "Villages of Yair". Rashi says he had no sons, so he gave them his name as a memorial.

sources.quote: חותיהם. פירושו לפי מקומו כמו קריות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word means towns or villages.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ לוֹ בָנִים קְרָאַתָם בִּשְׁמוֹ לְזִכָּרוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says because he had no sons, he called the villages by his name as a memorial.

32:42.headline: A missing dot hints the new name did not last
32:42.body: Novach called the town by his own name. The word לה, "it", lacks the usual dot in its last letter. A teacher Rashi quotes reads this as "not": the name did not stick. Rashi is not convinced, since other verses spell it the same way.

sources.quote: אֵינוֹ מַפִּיק הֵ"א, וְרָאִיתִי בִיסוֹדוֹ שֶׁל רַ' מֹשֶׁה הַדַּרְשָׁן לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַיֵּם לָהּ שֵׁם זֶה לְפִיכָךְ הוּא רָפֶה, שֶׁמַּשְׁמָעוּת מִדְרָשׁוֹ כְּמוֹ לֹא
sources.says: Rashi says the ה has no dot, and quotes Rabbi Moshe HaDarshan: the name did not last, so the word reads like "not".

sources.quote: וּתְמֵהַנִי מַה יִּדְרֹשׁ בִּשְׁתֵּי תֵבוֹת הַדּוֹמוֹת לָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says he wonders how that teacher would explain two other words spelled the same way.

sources.quote: רפה ע״‎י שלא קרא לה נבח אלא לפי שעה עד שובו מעבר הירדן להודיע שהיא היתה שלו
sources.says: Chizkuni says the word is soft because Novach gave the name only for a time, to show the town was his until he came back across the Jordan.

33:15.headline: Sinai gained a tenth letter for the Ten Commandments
33:15.body: Chizkuni says the Sinai desert is the same as the Sin desert. It gained the letter yod, whose number value is ten, because the Ten Commandments were given there.

sources.quote: והוא מדבר סין ועל שם ששם נתנו עליו עשרת הדברות נתווסף אות עשירי בשמו
sources.says: Chizkuni says it is the Sin desert, and because the Ten Commandments were given there, a tenth letter was added to its name.

33:38.headline: Aaron died 'by the mouth of God': by a kiss
33:38.body: The phrase על פי ה' usually means 'at God's command'. Here פי is read literally as 'mouth'. Rashi says it teaches that Aaron died by a kiss.

sources.quote: מלמד שמת בנשיקה
sources.says: Rashi says it teaches that Aaron died by a kiss.

33:52.headline: Stone floors laid down for bowing to idols
33:52.body: Rashi follows Onkelos: these are 'houses of bowing'. He says they covered the ground with marble floors so people could lie flat on them in worship.

sources.quote: על שם שהיו מסככין את הקרקע ברצפת אבנים של שיש להשתחוות עליהם
sources.says: Rashi says they were named for covering the ground with marble paving to bow down on.

sources.quote: ית כל בית סגדתהון
sources.says: Onkelos translates 'all their houses of bowing'.

33:55.headline: A thorn hedge that hems you in, or a whip at your side
33:55.body: Rashi says צנינם is a hedge of thorns that closes you in so you cannot come or go. Ibn Ezra offers whips or sharp thorns. Rashbam says it is another kind of thorn.

sources.quote: לשון מסוכת קוצים הסוככת אתכם, לסגר ולכלא אתכם מאין יוצא ובא
sources.says: Rashi says it means a thorn hedge around you that shuts you in so none can go out or come in.

sources.quote: שהם מכות בשוט או קוצים חדים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they are lashes of a whip or sharp thorns.

sources.quote: גם הוא ממיני קוצים המזיקים לבני אדם
sources.says: Rashbam says it too is a kind of thorn that hurts people.

34:2.headline: The land "falls" to you: by lot, or by a fallen angel
34:2.body: Rashi and Sforno say land handed out by lot is said to "fall", because lots are cast. The midrash asks how land can fall, and answers that God threw down the land's guardian angel before Israel.

sources.quote: עַל שֵׁם שֶׁנִּתְחַלְּקָה בְגוֹרָל נִקְרֵאת חֲלֻקָּה לְשׁוֹן נְפִילָה
sources.says: Rashi says that because the land was divided by lot, the sharing out is called falling.

sources.quote: כִּי בְגוֹרָל יָאוֹת לְשׁוֹן נְפִילָה, כְּמוֹ ״וְעַל לְבוּשִׁי יַפִּילוּ גוֹרָל״
sources.says: Sforno says the word "fall" fits a lot, as in "they cast lots for my clothing".

sources.quote: זאת הארץ אשר תפל לכם בנחלה. וכי הארץ נופלת. והלא כתיב: והארץ לעולם עומדת
sources.says: The midrash asks how the land can fall, since Scripture says the earth stands forever.

sources.quote: נטל שר הארץ וכפתו והפילו לפניהם
sources.says: The midrash answers that God took the land's guardian angel, tied him up and threw him down before them.

34:6.headline: One extra word adds the islands in the sea
34:6.body: After naming the Great Sea as the western border, the verse adds "and border", and Rashi says this makes the islands in the sea part of the land. Bekhor Shor says the islands have trees, so from afar they look like ships with sails.

sources.quote: הַנִּסִּין שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ הַיָּם אַף הֵם מִן הַגְּבוּל
sources.says: Rashi says the islands in the sea are also part of the border.

sources.quote: לפי שיש בהם באותם איים אלנות ונראי' כספינה שיש עליה נס בתוך הים
sources.says: Bekhor Shor says the islands have trees, so they look like a ship with a sail in the sea.

34:15.headline: East is the "front" of the world
34:15.body: קדמה means eastward, and its root also means front. Rashi says east is the face of the world and west its back, so south is on the right and north on the left.

sources.quote: שֶׁרוּחַ מִזְרָחִית קְרוּיָה פָנִים וּמַעֲרָבִית קְרוּיָה אָחוֹר, לְפִיכָךְ דָּרוֹם לַיָּמִין וְצָפוֹן לַשְּׂמֹאל
sources.says: Rashi says east is called the front and west the back, so south is to the right and north to the left.

34:17.headline: "Inherit for you": the leaders take the land on your behalf
34:17.body: The verb is ינחלו, they will inherit, and Rashi says each tribal leader takes the land for his tribe as its agent. Chizkuni reads it as ינחילו, they will hand it out.

sources.quote: יִנְחֲלוּ מַשְׁמַע שֶׁהֵם נוֹחֲלִים לָכֶם — בִּשְׁבִילְכֶם וּבִמְקוֹמְכֶם
sources.says: Rashi says ינחלו means they take the inheritance for you, in your place.

sources.quote: כָּל נָשִׂיא וְנָשִׂיא אַפּוֹטְרוֹפּוֹס לְשִׁבְטוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says each chieftain acts as guardian for his tribe.

sources.quote: [אשר ינחלו כמו ינחילו]
sources.says: Chizkuni says ינחלו is like ינחילו, they will hand out.

34:21.headline: The midrash says Elidad is Eldad the prophet
34:21.body: The midrash says Elidad son of Kislon is Eldad, who prophesied in the camp, and that Medad is Kemuel son of Shiftan. Rabbeinu Bahya says a prophet did not need the title chieftain, so Elidad is not given it.

sources.quote: אלדד, הוא אלידד בן כסלון. ומידד, זה קמואל בן שפטן
sources.says: The midrash says Eldad is Elidad son of Kislon, and Medad is Kemuel son of Shiftan.

sources.quote: וכיון שהיה נביא לא הוצרך הכתוב לקראו נשיא
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says that since he was a prophet, the text did not need to call him chieftain.

35:25.headline: The killer goes free when the high priest dies, or the judge?
35:25.body: Rashi says the high priest brings God's presence and long life, and the killer cut life short. Or the priest should have prayed that this not happen. Rashbam says that by the plain sense it means the chief judge.

sources.quote: שֶׁהוּא בָא לְהַשְׁרוֹת שְׁכִינָה בְיִשְׂרָאֵל וּלְהַאֲרִיךְ יְמֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the high priest comes to bring God's presence to Israel and lengthen their days.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל לְהִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁלֹּא תֶאֱרַע תַּקָּלָה זוֹ
sources.says: Rashi's second reason: the high priest should have prayed that this disaster not happen.

sources.quote: לפי פשוטו: כל ימי השופט הגדול
sources.says: Rashbam says by the plain sense it means all the days of the chief judge.

35:32.headline: לנוס means 'one who already fled', not 'to flee'
35:32.body: Rashi stops on the form. He reads לנוס as a name for someone who has already fled, like 'those back from war'. If it meant 'to flee', the verse could not go on to speak of returning home.

sources.quote: כֵּן תֹּאמַר לָנוּס עַל מִי שֶׁנָּס כְּבָר
sources.says: Rashi says לנוס is said of someone who has already fled.

sources.quote: לֹא יָדַעְתִּי הֵיאַךְ יֹאמַר לָשׁוּב לָשֶׁבֶת בָּאָרֶץ, הֲרֵי עֲדַיִן לֹא נָס
sources.says: Rashi says if it meant 'to flee', the verse could not say 'to return', since he has not fled yet.

35:33.headline: Do not make the land guilty, or do not flatter?
35:33.body: Rashi follows Onkelos: do not make the land guilty. Ibn Ezra and Rabbeinu Bahya say חנף means doing wrong in secret. The Sifrei reads it as a warning against flatterers.

sources.quote: לֹא תַרְשִׁיעוּ, כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'do not make guilty', as Onkelos translates.

sources.quote: העושה רע בסתר יקרא חנף
sources.says: Bahya says one who does wrong in secret is called חנף.

sources.quote: ולא תחניפו הארץ - הרי אזהרה לחניפים
sources.says: The Sifrei says this verse is a warning to flatterers.

35:33.headline: Rabbi Yoshiya splits יחניף into 'anger rests on the land'
35:33.body: The Sifrei reports that Rabbi Yoshiya read יחניף as two words, יחון אף: spilled blood makes anger settle on the land.

sources.quote: ר' יאשיה היה אומר לשון נוטריקון: כי הדם יחון אף בארץ
sources.says: The Sifrei says Rabbi Yoshiya read it as an acronym: the blood makes anger rest on the land.

4:22.headline: 'Lift the head' means count, and also raise up
4:22.body: נשא את ראש, 'lift the head', is a way of saying 'count'. Kli Yakar and Or HaChaim note it is used for Kohath and Gershon but not for Merari, because lifting the head also means raising someone's rank.

sources.quote: ונאמר לשון נשא בבני קהת ובבני גרשון, ולא בבני מררי, לפי שהיה לשניהם מעלה ביתר שאת על בני מררי
sources.says: Kli Yakar says the word נשא is used for Kohath and Gershon, not Merari, because both had higher standing than Merari.

sources.quote: שינשא וירומם בני גרשון לערך בני מררי
sources.says: Or HaChaim says the word means God raised Gershon above Merari.

4:47.headline: 'The work of work': music for the offerings
4:47.body: עבדת עבדה, 'the work of work', is an odd phrase. Rashi and Bahya say it is the Levites' music, a service that goes with another service, the offerings, while Chizkuni says it is taking down and putting up the Tabernacle.

sources.quote: עבדת עבדה. היא השיר במצלתים וכנורות, שהיא עבודה לעבודה אחרת
sources.says: Rashi says it is the song with cymbals and harps, a service for another service.

sources.quote: זה השיר שהיה עבודה לעבודה אחרת והיא הקרבנות
sources.says: Bahya says it is the song, which served another service, the offerings.

sources.quote: לעבד עבדת עבדה הורדת והקמת המשכן
sources.says: Chizkuni says it means taking down and putting up the Tabernacle.

5:12.headline: Straying from the path, and a spirit of folly
5:12.body: Plainly תשטה means the wife turns aside from modest ways, but the sages hear שטות, folly, in it: no one commits adultery unless a spirit of folly enters them. Kli Yakar even hears תשתה, 'she drinks', since ט and ת can swap.

sources.quote: אין המנאפין נואפין עד שתכנס בהן רוח שטות, דכתיב "כי תשטה"
sources.says: Rashi quotes the sages that adulterers do not sin until a spirit of folly enters them, reading it from תשטה.

sources.quote: ופשוטו של מקרא: כי תשטה — תט מדרכי צניעות
sources.says: Rashi says the plain meaning is that she turns aside from modest ways.

sources.quote: כי ״תשטה״ בטי״ת כמו ״תשתה״ בתי״ו
sources.says: Kli Yakar suggests that תשטה with a ט is like תשתה, 'she drinks', with a ת.

5:13.headline: 'Not caught', or 'not forced'?
5:13.body: נתפשה can mean 'caught' or 'seized'. Ibn Ezra reads 'she was not caught' by witnesses, while Rashi and Rashbam read 'she was not forced', so the law covers only a willing act.

sources.quote: נתפשה. נאנסה, כמו "ותפשה ושכב עמה"
sources.says: Rashi says the word means forced, as in the verse about a man who seizes a girl.

sources.quote: והיא לא נתפשה - לא נאנסה
sources.says: Rashbam says it means she was not forced.

sources.quote: והיא לא נתפשה. בעדים אנשים או על ידי נשים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means she was not caught by witnesses, men or women.

5:14.headline: Not just jealousy, but a formal warning
5:14.body: וקנא sounds like 'he was jealous'. Rashi and Sforno say the sages read it as a warning: the husband tells his wife not to be alone with a certain man.

sources.quote: פרשו רבותינו לשון התראה, שמתרה בה, אל תסתרי עם איש פלוני
sources.says: Rashi says the sages explain it as a warning: he warns her not to be alone with a certain man.

sources.quote: וקנא את אשתו. התרה בה ואמר: אל תסתרי עם איש פלוני
sources.says: Sforno says it means he warned her not to be alone with a certain man.

5:15.headline: No incense, because the mothers are called incense
5:15.body: Most grain offerings carry לבנה, frankincense, but this one does not. Rashi says the Matriarchs are called 'the hill of frankincense' in the Song of Songs, and this woman turned from their ways.

sources.quote: שהאמהות נקראו לבונה, שנאמר "ואל גבעת הלבונה"
sources.says: Rashi says the Matriarchs are called frankincense, from the verse 'to the hill of frankincense'.

sources.quote: והיא פרשה מדרכיהן
sources.says: Rashi says this woman turned away from their ways.

5:21.headline: Her name becomes the words of an oath
5:21.body: What does it mean to become 'a curse and an oath'? Rashi and Rashbam say people will use her story when they curse or swear: 'may it happen to me as it happened to her'.

sources.quote: שיהיו הכל נשבעין ביך
sources.says: Rashi says everyone will swear by her.

sources.quote: שאם תכזב בי תהיה מקולל, כאשה פלונית שצבתה בטנה ונפלה ירכה
sources.says: Rashbam says a person will make another swear: if you lie, may you be cursed like the woman whose belly swelled.

5:21.headline: The thigh, or the womb?
5:21.body: ירך usually means thigh, but Chizkuni says here it means the womb, as in 'those who came out of Jacob's ירך'. Rashi notes the curse names it before the belly, because the sin began there.

sources.quote: ירכך היא בית הרחם דוגמא תחת ירכי יוצאי ירך יעקב
sources.says: Chizkuni says the word means the womb, as in 'those who came out of Jacob's thigh'.

sources.quote: בקללה הקדים ירך לבטן, לפי שבה התחילה בעברה תחלה
sources.says: Rashi says the curse names the thigh before the belly because the sin started with it.

6:2.headline: Yafli: to set oneself apart, or to do something wondrous
6:2.body: Rashi and Onkelos read יפלא as 'set apart'. Ibn Ezra adds a second sense from פלא, 'wonder': taking this vow is remarkable, since most people follow their desires.

sources.quote: כי יפלא. יַפְרִישׁ
sources.says: Rashi says yafli means 'sets apart'.

sources.quote: אֲרֵי יְפָרֵשׁ לְמִדַּר נְדַר נְזִירוּ
sources.says: Onkelos renders: when he sets himself apart to vow a nazirite vow.

sources.quote: יפלא. יפריש או יעשה דבר פלא כי רוב העולם הולכים אחר תאותם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means sets apart, or does a wondrous thing, since most of the world follows its desires.

6:3.headline: Shechar: any strong drink, or simply old wine?
6:3.body: Rashi follows Onkelos, 'new wine and old', since wine makes one drunk when it is old. Ibn Ezra also brings the view that שכר is anything that makes a person drunk.

sources.quote: מֵחֲמַר חֲדַת וְעַתִּיק יִזַּר
sources.says: Onkelos renders: from new wine and old he shall abstain.

sources.quote: שֶׁהַיַּיִן מְשַׁכֵּר כְּשֶׁהוּא יָשָׁן
sources.says: Rashi says wine intoxicates when it is old.

sources.quote: ואחרים אמרו שכר ממש כל דבר שישתכר האדם ממנו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says others hold that shechar is anything a person gets drunk from.

6:3.headline: Mishrat: a word found only here, grapes soaked or loosened
6:3.body: Rashi says משרת means soaking in water or any drink, as the Mishnah speaks of a nazir who soaked his bread in wine. Rashbam takes it as whatever comes loose and falls from the grapes, like a man freed from his chains.

sources.quote: משרת. אין לו חבר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word has no partner elsewhere.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן צְבִיעָה בְּמַיִם וְכָל מַשְׁקֶה
sources.says: Rashi says it means steeping in water or any liquid.

sources.quote: נָזִיר שֶׁשָּׁרָה פִתּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi cites the Mishnah: a nazir who soaked his bread.

sources.quote: כל מה שנבדל ונופל מן הענבים, כאדם הנבדל וניתר מקשר הכבלים והזיקים שקשור בהם
sources.says: Rashbam says it is whatever separates and falls from the grapes, like a man released from the chains that bound him.

6:4.headline: Chartzanim: the seeds, or the skins?
6:4.body: Both חרצנים and זג appear only in this verse. Rashi says חרצנים are the seeds; Ibn Ezra reports commentators who had it the other way round.

sources.quote: חרצנים. הֵם הַגַּרְעִינִין
sources.says: Rashi says chartzanim are the seeds.

sources.quote: מחרצנים. אין לו ריע וכן זג והמפרשים אמרו חרצנים חצונים וזג פנימי' ואחרים הפכו הפירוש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says neither word has a partner; the commentators said chartzanim are the outer part and zag the inner, and others reversed it.

sources.quote: ומלת חרצנים אין לה חבר בכל המקרא, וכן מלת זג
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says neither chartzanim nor zag appears anywhere else in Scripture.

6:7.headline: Nezer: the crown of his God on his head
6:7.body: Onkelos renders נזר as a crown: 'the crown of his God is on his head'. Ibn Ezra and Rabbeinu Bahya draw the lesson: the true king is the one free of his desires, while other people are their slaves.

sources.quote: אֲרֵי כְּלִילָא דֶאֱלָהֵיהּ עַל רֵישֵׁיהּ
sources.says: Onkelos renders: for the crown of his God is on his head.

sources.quote: ויש אומרים כי מלת נזיר מגזרת נזר והעד כי נזר אלהיו על ראשו ואיננו רחוק
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some derive nazir from nezer, crown, citing this verse, and that this is not far-fetched.

sources.quote: והמלך באמת שיש לו נזר ועטרת מלכות בראשו כל מי שהוא חפשי מן התאות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the true king, with a royal crown on his head, is anyone free of desires.

sources.quote: ונקרא בשם הזה על שם שהוא מלך מולך על התאוות הפך משאר בני העולם שהם עבדי התאוות
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says he is called so because he rules over his desires, unlike others who are their slaves.

6:9.headline: Petha pitom: an accident, a mistake, or even on purpose?
6:9.body: Rashi reads פתע as an accident beyond one's control and פתאום as an honest mistake, though some say the two words mean one thing. Rabbeinu Bahya cites the rabbis who read פתאם as on purpose, from פתאים, 'fools'.

sources.quote: בפתע. זֶה אֹנֶס
sources.says: Rashi says petha means something forced, beyond his control.

sources.quote: פתאום. זֶה שׁוֹגֵג, וְיֵ"א פֶּתַע פִּתְאֹם דָּבָר אֶחָד הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says pitom means by mistake, and some say petha pitom is one thing.

sources.quote: נאמר בנזיר בפתע שהוא שוגג, פתאם הוא מזיד, לפי שנאמר (משלי כב) ופתאים עברו ונענשו
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya cites the rabbis: petha is by mistake and pitom is on purpose, from 'fools pass on and are punished'.

6:11.headline: How did the nazir 'sin against his soul'?
6:11.body: Rashi gives the plain sense: he was not careful to avoid the dead. He also cites Rabbi Elazar HaKappar: his sin was making himself suffer by giving up wine.

sources.quote: שֶׁלֹּא נִזְהַר מִטֻּמְאַת הַמֵּת
sources.says: Rashi says he was not careful about impurity from the dead.

sources.quote: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר אוֹמֵר, שֶׁצִּעֵר עַצְמוֹ מִן הַיַּיִן
sources.says: Rashi cites Rabbi Elazar HaKappar: he caused himself pain by keeping from wine.

sources.quote: על הנפש. הוא על נפש מת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'the soul' here means a dead body.

6:14.headline: Why a sin offering for finishing a holy vow?
6:14.body: Ramban says the nazir 'sins' by ending his term, because he steps down from holiness; he ought to have stayed a nazir all his life. Rabbeinu Bahya says even so the law is unusual, since no other offering is brought for something still to come.

sources.quote: כִּי הָאִישׁ הַזֶּה חוֹטֵא נַפְשׁוֹ בִּמְלֹאת הַנְּזִירוּת, כִּי הוּא עַתָּה נָזוֹר מִקְּדֻשָּׁתוֹ וַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם
sources.says: Ramban says this man sins against himself when his term ends, for he now turns away from his holiness and God's service.

sources.quote: וְרָאוּי הָיָה לוֹ שֶׁיַּזִּיר לְעוֹלָם
sources.says: Ramban says he should rightly have stayed a nazir forever.

sources.quote: ועם כל הטעם הזה לא יצא קרבנו של נזיר מן החדוש כי היכן מצינו קרבן על העתיד
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says that even with this reason the offering stays unique, for where else is an offering brought for the future?

6:23.headline: Ko, 'thus': the manner of the blessing, and the number 25
6:23.body: Rabbeinu Bahya cites the rabbis: 'thus' (כה) fixes the manner, with raised hands, in Hebrew, standing, aloud, face to face, and with God's Name. He adds that כה has the value 25: the blessing joins the priests' 24 gifts.

sources.quote: ודרשו רז"ל כה תברכו בנשיאות כפים, כה תברכו בלשון הקדש, כה תברכו בעמידה, כה תברכו בקול רם, כה תברכו פנים כנגד פנים, כה תברכו בשם המפורש
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya cites the rabbis: bless with raised hands, in the holy tongue, standing, aloud, face to face, and with the explicit Name.

sources.quote: ולפי שעתיד למסור להם ארבעה ועשרים מתנות כהונה ועם זו הם עשרים וחמשה, לכך הזכיר הלשון הזה כ"ה תברכו
sources.says: He says that since the priests would receive 24 gifts, and with this one they make 25, the Torah says 'ko', which equals 25.

6:23.headline: Amor, spelled in full: bless with a whole heart
6:23.body: Rashi notes that אמור is written in full. The midrash he cites learns that the priests must not bless in a rush, but with intent and a whole heart; he adds that all the people must be able to hear.

sources.quote: אמור. מָלֵא — לֹא תְבָרְכֵם בְּחִפָּזוֹן וּבַהֲלוּת, אֶלָּא בְכַוָּנָה וּבְלֵב שָׁלֵם
sources.says: Rashi says amor is spelled full: do not bless them hastily, but with intent and a whole heart.

sources.quote: אמור להם. שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כֻלָּם שׁוֹמְעִים
sources.says: Rashi says 'say to them' means so that all can hear.

6:24.headline: A blessing no robber can take
6:24.body: Rashi says a human giver cannot protect his gift from thieves, but God both gives and guards. Ibn Ezra reads it the same way: He keeps what He added, so no one takes it.

sources.quote: שֶׁהַנּוֹתֵן מַתָּנָה לְעַבְדּוֹ אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְשָׁמְרוֹ מִכָּל אָדָם
sources.says: Rashi says one who gives his servant a gift cannot guard it from everyone.

sources.quote: אֲבָל הַקָּבָּ"ה, הוּא הַנּוֹתֵן, הוּא הַשּׁוֹמֵר
sources.says: Rashi says God is both the giver and the guard.

sources.quote: וטעם וישמרך. שישמור התוספת שלא יגזול אחר מה שהוסיף
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says He will guard the added good so that no one robs it.

6:25.headline: 'May He shine His face': a smile, or His Presence's light?
6:25.body: Rashi reads it as a warm, smiling face turned toward you. Onkelos, and Ramban citing Rabbi Natan, read it as the light of God's Presence shining on you.

sources.quote: יַרְאֶה לְךָ פָּנִים שׂוֹחֲקוֹת, פָּנִים צְהֻבּוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says He will show you a smiling, bright face.

sources.quote: יַנְהַר יְיָ שְׁכִנְתֵּיהּ לְוָתָךְ
sources.says: Onkelos renders: may the Lord make His Presence shine toward you.

sources.quote: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: זֶה מְאוֹר שְׁכִינָה
sources.says: Ramban cites Rabbi Natan: this is the light of the Divine Presence.

6:26.headline: 'May He lift His face': calm His anger, or watch over you?
6:26.body: Rashi reads it as 'may He hold back His anger', and Maimonides says 'face' here means God's care staying with us. Rashbam squares it with 'who shows no favor' (Deuteronomy 10:17): God does not excuse sin, but turns toward the one He loves.

sources.quote: ישא ה' פניו אליך. יִכְבֹּשׁ כַּעֲסוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means He will suppress His anger.

sources.quote: פנים הוא גם שם החסות וההשגחה
sources.says: Maimonides says 'face' is also a word for protection and providence.

sources.quote: והכוונה להתלוות השגחתו עלינו
sources.says: He says the verse means that God's providence will accompany us.

sources.quote: הקב"ה לא ישא פני איש לנקותו מכל פשעיו, אבל הוא ישא פנים שלו את אהובו שיפנה אליו לחננו
sources.says: Rashbam says God will not show favor to clear a person of all his sins, but will lift His own face to the one He loves, turning to be gracious to him.

6:27.headline: 'And I will bless them': Israel, or the priests?
6:27.body: Rashi gives both readings: God blesses Israel, agreeing with the priests, or God blesses the priests themselves. Ibn Ezra holds that 'them' means everyone, priests and Israel alike.

sources.quote: לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאַסְכִּים עִם הַכֹּהֲנִים; דָּ"אַ, וַאֲנִי אֲבָרְכֵם — לַכֹּהֲנִים
sources.says: Rashi says: I will bless Israel and agree with the priests; another reading, I will bless the priests.

sources.quote: לפי דעתי שמ"ם אברכם סימן לכלם כהנים וישראלים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says in his view 'them' refers to all of them, priests and Israelites.

sources.quote: כשיברכו הכהנים לישראל בשמי ולא בשמם, אני אברכם לישראל
sources.says: Rashbam says when the priests bless Israel in God's name and not their own, God blesses Israel.

7:1.headline: The day Moses 'finished' sounds like the day of a bride
7:1.body: Rashi says the word is written כלת, close to כלה, a bride: the day the Tabernacle stood, Israel was like a bride entering her wedding canopy. He also reads it plainly. For seven days Moses set it up and took it down, and on this day his setting-up was finished. Or HaChaim notes that Torah scrolls actually spell the word with the vav.

sources.quote: יוֹם הֲקָמַת הַמִּשְׁכָּן הָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּכַלָּה הַנִּכְנֶסֶת לַחֻפָּה
sources.says: Rashi says on the day the Tabernacle was set up, Israel was like a bride entering the wedding canopy.

sources.quote: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם כָּלוּ הֲקָמוֹתָיו
sources.says: Rashi says on that day his settings-up came to an end.

sources.quote: וְרוֹאַנִי כִּי בְּסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה כְּתוּבָה בְּוָא״ו
sources.says: Or HaChaim says he sees that in the Torah scroll the word is written with a vav.

7:19.headline: A silver bowl that counts the years of Adam
7:19.body: Each chief brings the same gifts, and Rashi, following Rabbi Moshe HaDarshan, reads them as symbols. The letters of קערת כסף add up to 930, the years Adam lived. The bowl weighs 130, his age when he fathered Seth.

sources.quote: מִנְיַן אוֹתִיוֹתָיו בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא תתק"ל, כְּנֶגֶד שְׁנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says the letters add up to 930, matching the years of Adam.

sources.quote: וַיְחִי אָדָם שְׁלֹשִׁים וּמְאַת שָׁנָה וַיּוֹלֶד
sources.says: Rashi says the weight of 130 recalls that Adam was 130 when he had a son.

sources.quote: עַד כָּאן בִּיסוֹדוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֹשֶׁה הַדַּרְשָׁן
sources.says: Rashi says these readings come from the work of Rabbi Moshe HaDarshan.

7:48.headline: Ephraim's chief carries Joseph's refusal in his name
7:48.body: Ephraim is Joseph's son. The midrash reads אלישמע as 'to Me he listened', and not to his mistress, Potiphar's wife. It reads his father's name עמיהוד as 'his glory was with Me'.

sources.quote: אֱלִישָׁמָע, אֵלַי שָׁמַע, וְלַאֲדוֹנָתוֹ לֹא שָׁמַע
sources.says: The midrash says Elishama means 'to Me he listened', and he did not listen to his mistress.

sources.quote: עַמִּיהוּד, עִמִּי הָיָה הוֹדוֹ
sources.says: The midrash says Ammihud means 'his glory was with Me'.

7:54.headline: Manasseh's chief: 'God repaid me', 'the Rock freed me'
7:54.body: Manasseh is also Joseph's son. The midrash hears Joseph speaking in the names. גמליאל: God repaid me with good. פדהצור: the Rock freed me from prison.

sources.quote: גַּמְלִיאֵל, גָּמַל אֵל עִמִּי גְּמוּלִים טוֹבִים
sources.says: The midrash has Joseph say Gamliel means God did good things for me.

sources.quote: פָּדַנִי צוּר מִצָּרָתִי מִבֵּית הַסֹּהַר
sources.says: The midrash says Pedahtzur means the Rock freed me from my trouble, from prison.

7:72.headline: Why 'eleven' is the odd word עשתי עשר
7:72.body: Hebrew normally says אחד עשר for eleven. Ibn Ezra ties עשתי to עשתנות, thoughts, as if ten had given birth to one more. He rejects Rabbi Yonah, who built it on שתי, two, as 'the number before twelve'.

sources.quote: כמו עשתנותיו מה שיולידו מחשבותיו כאילו העשר הוליד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is like עשתנותיו, what thoughts give birth to, as if ten gave birth.

sources.quote: ויאמר רבי יונה הספרדי כי פירושו על שתי עשר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports that Rabbi Yonah read it as built on שתי, two, and says he was wrong.

7:89.headline: God was speaking to Himself, and Moses overheard
7:89.body: The verse says מִדַּבֵּר, an unusual form, instead of the plain מְדַבֵּר. Rashi reads it as מתדבר, 'speaking with Himself': out of respect for God, the voice speaks and Moses hears it. Ibn Ezra notes the grammar debate about this form.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ מִתְדַּבֵּר, כְּבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל מַעְלָה לוֹמַר כֵּן
sources.says: Rashi says it is like מתדבר, a respectful way to speak of God.

sources.quote: מְדַּבֵּר בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין עַצְמוֹ, וּמֹשֶׁה שׁוֹמֵעַ מֵאֵלָיו
sources.says: Rashi says God speaks with Himself, and Moses hears on his own.

sources.quote: וכל המדקדקים אמרו כי מדבר אליו מבנין התפעל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the grammarians all held this is a reflexive verb form.

7:89.headline: 'The voice': the same voice heard at Sinai
7:89.body: The verse says 'the voice', with 'the'. Rashi and Bahya say it is the same voice that spoke at Sinai. Rashi adds that it stopped at the tent door and did not go outside.

sources.quote: הוּא הַקּוֹל שֶׁנִּדְבַּר עִמּוֹ בְּסִינַי
sources.says: Rashi says it is the voice that spoke with him at Sinai.

sources.quote: וּכְשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לַפֶּתַח הָיָה נִפְסָק
sources.says: Rashi says when it reached the doorway it stopped.

sources.quote: הוא הקול ששמע בסיני
sources.says: Bahya says it is the voice he heard at Sinai.

8:2.headline: 'When you raise the lamps' means when you light them
8:2.body: The verse says 'when you raise up' the lamps, where Onkelos simply says 'when you light'. Rashi says the word fits because the flame rises, so the priest must light until it climbs on its own, and the sages also read it as a step the priest went up.

sources.quote: עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהַלַּהַב עוֹלֶה, כָּתוּב בְּהַדְלָקָתָן לְשׁוֹן עֲלִיָּה
sources.says: Rashi says that because the flame rises, the lighting is described with a word for going up.

sources.quote: שֶׁמַּעֲלָה הָיְתָה לִפְנֵי הַמְּנוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says the sages also learned from it that there was a step in front of the menorah.

sources.quote: בְּאַדְלָקוּתָךְ יָת בּוֹצִינַיָּא
sources.says: Onkelos translates it 'when you light the lamps'.

8:4.headline: 'This is the menorah': God pointed it out
8:4.body: Rashi says the word 'this' means God showed Moses the menorah as if pointing with a finger, because Moses found it hard to picture. Ibn Ezra says the verse tells us nothing like it had been seen before.

sources.quote: שֶׁהֶרְאָהוּ הַקָּבָּ"ה בְּאֶצְבַּע, לְפִי שֶׁנִּתְקַשָּׁה בָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says God showed it to Moses with a finger, because Moses had trouble with it.

sources.quote: וזה מעשה המנורה. הזכיר שלא נראה כמוהו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the verse mentions that its like had never been seen.

8:4.headline: Beaten from one block of gold
8:4.body: Rashi reads מקשה from the Aramaic in Daniel, where knees 'knocked' one against the other. The menorah was hammered out of a single block of gold, not built from parts joined together.

sources.quote: עֶשֶׁת שֶׁל כִּכַּר זָהָב הָיְתָה, וּמַקִּישׁ בְּקֻרְנָס
sources.says: Rashi says it was a block of gold that the smith beat with a hammer, from the Aramaic word for knocking.

8:6.headline: You 'take' people by talking to them
8:6.body: You cannot take people the way you take an object. Rashi says 'take' here means winning the Levites over with words, telling them how lucky they are to serve God, and Onkelos translates it 'bring near'.

sources.quote: קָחֵם בִּדְבָרִים — אַשְׁרֵיכֶם שֶׁתִּזְכּוּ לִהְיוֹת שַׁמָּשִׁים לַמָּקוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says to take them with words: how fortunate you are to become servants of God.

sources.quote: קָרֵב יָת לֵוָאֵי
sources.says: Onkelos translates it 'bring the Levites near'.

8:16.headline: 'Given, given': why the word is said twice
8:16.body: The verse says the Levites are 'given, given' to God. Rashi says they were given for two jobs, carrying the Tabernacle and singing, while Ibn Ezra says it means they and their children.

sources.quote: נְתוּנִים לְמַשָּׂא, נְתוּנִים לָשִׁיר
sources.says: Rashi says they were given for carrying and given for song.

sources.quote: כי נתונים נתונים. הם ובניהם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the doubled word means they and their sons.

8:24.headline: Twenty-five here, thirty elsewhere: when did Levites start?
8:24.body: Chapter 4 says the Levites begin work at thirty, but here it says twenty-five. Rashi says they spent five years learning and began serving at thirty, while Ibn Ezra says thirty was for carrying loads and twenty-five for work in the Tent.

sources.quote: בָּא לִלְמֹד הִלְכוֹת עֲבוֹדָה וְלוֹמֵד חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וּבֶן שְׁלֹשִׁים עוֹבֵד
sources.says: Rashi says at twenty-five a Levite came to learn the laws of the service, learned for five years, and served from thirty.

sources.quote: כי מבן שלשים שנה הוא לעבודת משא ומבן חמש ועשרים לעבודת האהל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says thirty is the age for carrying and twenty-five for the work of the Tent.

9:1.headline: Out of order, to spare Israel's shame
9:1.body: This happened in the first month, before the census that opens the book in the second month. Rashi says the Torah is not always in time order. The book did not open here because it is a shame to Israel: in forty years in the desert they brought only this one Passover.

sources.quote: פרשה שבראש הספר לא נאמרה עד איר, למדת שאין סדר מקדם ומאחר בתורה
sources.says: Rashi says the passage at the start of the book was not said until Iyar, so the Torah is not in time order.

sources.quote: מפני שהיא גנותן של ישראל, שכל ארבעים שנה שהיו ישראל במדבר לא הקריבו אלא פסח זו בלבד
sources.says: Rashi says it is Israel's shame, since in all forty years in the desert they offered only this Passover.

9:2.headline: 'At its set time', even on Shabbat
9:2.body: The sages read 'at its set time' as a firm rule. The Passover offering is brought on its day even when that day is Shabbat, and even when the people are impure.

sources.quote: במועדו. אף בשבת, במועדו — אף בטמאה
sources.says: Rashi says 'at its time' means even on Shabbat, and even in impurity.

9:7.headline: 'Why should we be left out?' earns them a new law
9:7.body: These men were impure and could not bring the offering, and they protested. Rashi says this law should have come through Moses like the rest of the Torah, but these men earned having it said because of them. Sforno says their impurity came from a good deed, so it should not lead them to miss one.

sources.quote: וראויה היתה פרשה זו לאמר ע"י משה כשאר כל התורה כלה, אלא שזכו אלו שתאמר על ידיהן
sources.says: Rashi says this section should have been said through Moses like all the Torah, but these men merited that it be said through them.

sources.quote: מאחר שהיתה טמאתנו לדבר מצוה, למה תהיה גוררת עבירה
sources.says: Sforno says they argued: since our impurity came from a commandment, why should it lead to a sin?

9:8.headline: 'Wait, and I will hear': Moses could ask God anytime
9:8.body: Moses tells the men to wait while he asks. Rashi says he spoke like a student sure his teacher will answer, and praises a person who could speak with God whenever he wished.

sources.quote: כתלמיד המבטח לשמע מפי רבו
sources.says: Rashi says Moses spoke like a student who is sure to hear from his teacher.

sources.quote: שכל זמן שהיה רוצה היה מדבר עם השכינה
sources.says: Rashi says whenever Moses wished, he spoke with the Divine Presence.

9:22.headline: 'Days' here means a whole year
9:22.body: The list goes two days, a month, then ימים, days. Rashi and Ibn Ezra say this last 'days' means a year, as in Leviticus 'his redemption is days', meaning a year.

sources.quote: או ימים. שנה, כמו "ימים תהיה גאלתו"
sources.says: Rashi says 'or days' means a year, as in 'days shall be his redemption'.

sources.quote: או ימים. שנה תמימה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'or days' means a full year.
